Avengers: Endgame.text: Out-earned Infinity War's entire theatrical run in eleven days.
Avengers: Endgame.evidence: It grossed $2.8 billion worldwide during its initial theatrical run, surpassing Infinity War's entire theatrical run in eleven days, setting several box-office records, and surpassing Avatar (2009) to become the highest-grossing film of all time.

Avatar.text: Planned for 1999, it waited because, Cameron said, the technology he needed did not exist yet.
Avatar.evidence: Filming was due to take place after the completion of Cameron's 1997 film Titanic, for a planned release in 1999; however, according to Cameron, the necessary technology was not yet available to achieve his vision of the film.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day.text: The title comes from a 2008 comic book storyline that reset Spider-Man's status quo.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day.evidence: McKenna and Sommers returned as writers by February 2023, Cretton was hired to direct by October 2024, and the title—derived from the 2008 comic book storyline "Brand New Day" that reset Spider-Man's status quo—was announced in March 2025.

Avatar: The Way of Water.text: New technology had to be developed to film its motion-capture scenes underwater.
Avatar: The Way of Water.evidence: However, the addition of two more sequels—for a total of five films—and the need to develop new technology to film motion-capture scenes underwater, led to significant delays.

Titanic.text: Production began in 1995 with James Cameron shooting footage of the real Titanic wreck.
Titanic.evidence: Production began on September 1, 1995, when Cameron shot footage of the Titanic wreck.

Ne Zha 2.text: The first animated film to cross $2 billion, made on a production budget of US$80 million.
Ne Zha 2.evidence: Like its predecessor, the film received highly positive reviews from critics, and achieved even greater commercial success at a gross of $2.2 billion worldwide against a production budget of US$80 million. ... Ne Zha 2 broke numerous box office records inside and outside China, including becoming the highest-grossing film in a single box office territory, the highest-grossing animated film, being the first adult animated film in this position, the highest-grossing non-English language film and the first animated film in history to cross the $2 billion mark, as well as being the highest-selling animated film based on ticket sales, overtaking The Jungle Book (1967).

Star Wars: The Force Awakens.text: The first Star Wars film not to extensively involve franchise creator George Lucas.
Star Wars: The Force Awakens.evidence: The film is the first Star Wars film to not extensively involve franchise creator George Lucas, who only served as a creative consultant in the early stages of production.

Avengers: Infinity War.text: The first superhero film to gross over $2 billion worldwide.

Spider-Man: No Way Home.text: Earlier Spider-Man actors Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield return, which the studios tried to hide until release.
Spider-Man: No Way Home.evidence: Several actors reprise their roles from those films, including previous Spider-Man actors Maguire and Garfield. The pair's involvement was the subject of wide speculation and numerous leaks despite Sony, Marvel, and the cast's efforts to conceal their involvement until the film's release.

Zootopia 2.text: The plot hinges on a snake turning up in Zootopia, where none had been seen for a century.
Zootopia 2.evidence: During a raid on a smuggling ring, Judy finds a piece of snake skin, although snakes have not been seen in Zootopia for a century. ... Meanwhile, a hooded creature crashes the party and reveals himself as a pit viper.
